**Subject: Application for Permission to Conduct Scientific Research in Reserved Forests – Reg.**

Dear Sir,

With reference to the above subject, we kindly request your permission to conduct scientific research and biodiversity surveys in the reserved forests of the Kanara Circle, specifically in the Dandeli and Anshi Tiger Reserve areas. The Western Ghats Conservation Initiative (WGCI) is a newly formed non-governmental organization established in 2015, and this will be our first major field research program.

The proposed study will focus on the distribution of large carnivores, particularly tigers and leopards, and their prey base. The methodology will include line transect surveys, camera trapping, and scat analysis. The data collected will be shared with the Forest Department for management planning purposes.

We have attached the detailed project proposal, the list of research personnel, and a copy of our registration for your perusal. We assure you that all ethical guidelines and legal requirements will be strictly adhered to.

We request you to consider our application favorably and grant the necessary permission at the earliest, as our field season is dependent on the pre-monsoon window (February to May).

Yours sincerely,

**(Dr. Ananya Rao)**

Sub: Submission of the All India Tiger Estimation (AITE) 2022-23 results for Kudremukh National Park – reg.

Sir,

The phase-wise enumeration for the All India Tiger Estimation 2022-23 (cycle 2022-2023) was carried out in Kudremukh National Park between 16.01.2023 and 12.02.2023. The field work was coordinated by the Kudremukh Wildlife Division in association with the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) and the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA). The data processing and analysis were performed at the WII, Dehradun. We are hereby submitting the final validated results for the park.

The summary of the estimation is provided below. The detailed methodology, transect-wise effort, and the camera trap photo capture records are enclosed as Annexures I to IV.

**1. ALL INDIA TIGER ESTIMATION (AITE) 2022-23 – SUMMARY RESULTS FOR KUDREMUKH NATIONAL PARK**

| Parameter | Result |
| :--- | :--- |
| Survey Period (Phase I) – Sign/Transect | 16.01.2023 to 24.01.2023 |
| Survey Period (Phase II) – Camera Trap | 28.01.2023 to 12.02.2023 |
| Total Area Covered (km²) | 600.32 |
| Number of Transects Walked | 32 |
| Total Transect Length (km) | 162.5 |
| Number of Camera Trap Locations | 74 |
| Total Camera Trap Nights | 1480 |
| Number of Individual Tigers Photo-captured | 22 (including 3 cubs) |
| Number of Unique Adult Tigers Identified | 19 |
| **Estimated Tiger Population (Current)** | **28 individuals** |

The All India Tiger Estimation reports that Kudremukh National Park has a tiger_count_2023 of 28 individuals. Record status: current. This figure is the final, current estimate for the year 2023 as per the national protocol and includes the adult breeding population, sub-adults, and cubs. The estimate is based on the standard double-sampling approach, using the capture-recapture analysis of camera trap data and extrapolation to the entire park area.

**2. METHODOLOGY**

The estimation followed the standard AITE protocol in three phases:

- **Phase I:** A systematic survey of 32 transects was carried out to collect data on tiger signs (pugmarks, scat, scratches) and prey abundance. The transects were distributed across the three ranges of the park: Kalsa, Someshwara, and Narasimharajapura.
- **Phase II:** Camera traps were deployed at 74 locations, primarily along water sources, trails, and ridge lines. The camera trap density was approximately one pair per 8-10 km². The traps were active for a period of 15 nights.
- **Phase III:** The data from Phases I and II were analyzed by the WII. The spatial capture-recapture model (SPACECAP) was used to estimate the density and abundance of tigers.

**3. RANGE-WISE DISTRIBUTION OF SIGNS (PHASE I)**

| Range | Transects | Pugmark Encounters | Scat Encounters | Prey (Chital/Sambar/Gaur) Encounters |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Kalsa | 12 | 18 | 9 | 47 |
| Someshwara | 11 | 14 | 6 | 38 |
| Narasimharajapura | 9 | 4 | 2 | 15 |

**4. CAMERA TRAP RESULTS (PHASE II)**

A total of 1480 camera trap nights were completed. The cameras yielded 234 independent captures of tigers. The individual identification was done based on the unique stripe patterns on the flanks and the hind legs. Of the 22 individuals photo-captured, 19 were adults (12 males, 7 females) and 3 were cubs. The capture-recapture analysis estimated a density of 4.66 tigers per 100 km², which when extrapolated to the 600.32 km² of the park, gives the final estimate of 28 individuals.

The camera trap locations with the highest capture rates were in the Kalsa range, particularly along the Bhadra River tributaries. The lowest capture rates were recorded in the Narasimharajapura range, which is more disturbed by anthropogenic pressures.

Following our discussions and your positive response, we are pleased to confirm your engagement as Consulting Veterinarian with the Western Ghats Conservation Initiative (WGCI). This letter sets out the terms of our collaboration.

**1. Scope of Work**

You will provide veterinary services to WGCI in connection with our wildlife monitoring and conservation programs in the Dandeli–Anshi Tiger Reserve landscape. Specific responsibilities include:

- Conducting health assessments of wildlife captured or handled during our field operations.
- Advising field teams on animal welfare protocols and handling procedures.
- Providing emergency veterinary support when required.

This agreement shall be effective from 01/04/2016 and shall remain in force for a period of two years, subject to renewal by mutual consent.

You shall maintain your registration with the Karnataka Veterinary Council for the duration of this agreement. Your current license (VET/KA/2018/221) has been verified with the Council and found to be current. Any change in your registration status must be communicated to us immediately.

**5. Confidentiality**

You agree to maintain confidentiality regarding all WGCI operational data, including animal locations, camera-trap placements, and survey results.

**6. Termination**

Either party may terminate this agreement with 30 days' written notice.

Please sign and return a copy of this letter to confirm your acceptance of these terms.

Yours sincerely,

Sub: Submission of the All India Tiger Estimation (AITE) 2022-23 results for Kudremukh National Park – reg.

Sir,

The phase-wise enumeration for the All India Tiger Estimation 2022-23 (cycle 2022-2023) was carried out in Kudremukh National Park between 16.01.2023 and 12.02.2023. The field work was coordinated by the Kudremukh Wildlife Division in association with the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) and the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA). The data processing and analysis were performed at the WII, Dehradun. We are hereby submitting the final validated results for the park.

The summary of the estimation is provided below. The detailed methodology, transect-wise effort, and the camera trap photo capture records are enclosed as Annexures I to IV.

**1. ALL INDIA TIGER ESTIMATION (AITE) 2022-23 – SUMMARY RESULTS FOR KUDREMUKH NATIONAL PARK**

| Parameter | Result |
| :--- | :--- |
| Survey Period (Phase I) – Sign/Transect | 16.01.2023 to 24.01.2023 |
| Survey Period (Phase II) – Camera Trap | 28.01.2023 to 12.02.2023 |
| Total Area Covered (km²) | 600.32 |
| Number of Transects Walked | 32 |
| Total Transect Length (km) | 162.5 |
| Number of Camera Trap Locations | 74 |
| Total Camera Trap Nights | 1480 |
| Number of Individual Tigers Photo-captured | 22 (including 3 cubs) |
| Number of Unique Adult Tigers Identified | 19 |
| **Estimated Tiger Population (Current)** | **28 individuals** |

The All India Tiger Estimation reports that Kudremukh National Park has a tiger_count_2023 of 28 individuals. Record status: current. This figure is the final, current estimate for the year 2023 as per the national protocol and includes the adult breeding population, sub-adults, and cubs. The estimate is based on the standard double-sampling approach, using the capture-recapture analysis of camera trap data and extrapolation to the entire park area.

**2. METHODOLOGY**

The estimation followed the standard AITE protocol in three phases:

- **Phase I:** A systematic survey of 32 transects was carried out to collect data on tiger signs (pugmarks, scat, scratches) and prey abundance. The transects were distributed across the three ranges of the park: Kalsa, Someshwara, and Narasimharajapura.
- **Phase II:** Camera traps were deployed at 74 locations, primarily along water sources, trails, and ridge lines. The camera trap density was approximately one pair per 8-10 km². The traps were active for a period of 15 nights.
- **Phase III:** The data from Phases I and II were analyzed by the WII. The spatial capture-recapture model (SPACECAP) was used to estimate the density and abundance of tigers.

**3. RANGE-WISE DISTRIBUTION OF SIGNS (PHASE I)**

| Range | Transects | Pugmark Encounters | Scat Encounters | Prey (Chital/Sambar/Gaur) Encounters |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Kalsa | 12 | 18 | 9 | 47 |
| Someshwara | 11 | 14 | 6 | 38 |
| Narasimharajapura | 9 | 4 | 2 | 15 |

**4. CAMERA TRAP RESULTS (PHASE II)**

A total of 1480 camera trap nights were completed. The cameras yielded 234 independent captures of tigers. The individual identification was done based on the unique stripe patterns on the flanks and the hind legs. Of the 22 individuals photo-captured, 19 were adults (12 males, 7 females) and 3 were cubs. The capture-recapture analysis estimated a density of 4.66 tigers per 100 km², which when extrapolated to the 600.32 km² of the park, gives the final estimate of 28 individuals.

The camera trap locations with the highest capture rates were in the Kalsa range, particularly along the Bhadra River tributaries. The lowest capture rates were recorded in the Narasimharajapura range, which is more disturbed by anthropogenic pressures.

All Range Forest Officers, Section Forest Officers, and Forest Guards of the Kalsa, Someshwara, and Narasimharajapura Ranges are hereby informed that, in view of the acute water scarcity anticipated during the months of April and May 2017, and the increased risk of human-wildlife conflict at water sources, the following restrictions shall be in force with immediate effect:

1.  No person, other than authorized forest staff, shall be permitted to enter the core zone of the tiger reserve between 18:00 hours and 06:00 hours.
2.  Grazing of cattle within the core zone is strictly prohibited from 01/04/2017.
3.  Collection of non-timber forest produce (NTFP) by fringe-area villagers under the Joint Forest Management (JFM) programme is suspended until further orders. The suspension is necessitated by the concentration of wild animals at the few remaining perennial water holes.

**Sub: Recording of wildlife mortality and cattle depredation cases – Regarding.**

All Range Forest Officers are directed to ensure that every case of wildlife mortality, including natural death, poaching, and road kill, is recorded in the prescribed register on the same day. The register must include the species, sex, approximate age, location (with GPS coordinates), and the probable cause of death. In cases where the cause cannot be ascertained in the field, the carcass shall be sent for post-mortem to the nearest veterinary institution and the report shall be attached to the case file.

Similarly, all cases of cattle depredation by tigers or leopards within the reserve or in the fringe villages shall be reported to this office within 24 hours. The Range Forest Officer shall verify the claim on the spot, record the details of the cattle owner, and issue a preliminary certificate. The final compensation amount will be decided by the Deputy Conservator of Forests based on the veterinary certificate and the market value of the cattle.

The existing practice of maintaining separate registers in each range is discontinued. A common mortality register will be maintained at the division office, and each range shall transmit the details by email or wireless message on a weekly basis.

Sd/-
